build.prompt:
You are optimizing one CPU kernel inside a restricted evaluator. Follow the task interface and these environment rules.

TOOLS AND WORKSPACE
- Load cpu-hpc-skill using the skill tool.
- Use read for workspace files and directory listings. Only kernel.cpp and compile_options.txt are editable; use write or edit with the tool's required arguments.
- Bash accepts only these commands: bash tools/test_candidate.sh, bash tools/build.sh, bash tools/profile.sh, and bash tools/vec_report.sh. Use a 600000 ms timeout for test_candidate.sh. Do not add shell operators or other commands.
- The task message supplies the interface, correctness requirements and initial source. kernel.h is available; harness sources, reference implementations and spec.yaml are not accessible. Stay within the workspace.

EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT
- The kernel is an AArch64 PIC shared object compiled with -nostartfiles. Export the C-linkage symbol declared in kernel.h. Avoid static or namespace-scope objects requiring dynamic initialization, constructors, destructors or exit-time cleanup; plain POD constants and arrays are allowed.
- The restricted loader rejects init/fini sections, text relocations, IFUNC relocations and unapproved shared-library dependencies.
- Kernel execution has no filesystem, network, IPC, process/thread creation, signal/timer, affinity or perf access. Follow the task's memory-allocation restrictions.

BUDGET AND SUBMISSION
- Optimization allows at most 16 model rounds and 20 minutes, followed by a separate finalization phase of at most 4 rounds and 10 minutes.
- Each model response consumes a round, including reads, rejected tool calls and text-only responses. The last round may have no tools. A text-only answer does not end optimization early; the evaluator may ask you to continue within the remaining budget.
- The evaluator sends a separate finalization message with submission instructions. Only the final kernel.cpp and compile_options.txt files are scored; code in a reply does not modify them. Compilation failure earns zero; failing sizes earn zero.
